proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the corrected hard-floor minimax value with matching converse and attainment, characterized the plateau and strict optimizer faces, and strengthened the balanced case to an exact all-even-N constant-shift radius plus six-moment compression. The mathematics and decision panels passed, but the novelty review capped the package at subfield because its gain over nearby endpoints is narrow and potentially second order. A structural classification of arbitrary nonconstant shifts and nonuniform balanced laws remains open and would require a new research advance rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: For even \(N\) with at least \(r\) units in each arm, the proposed hard-floor affine-equivariant saddle has normalized value \(V(N,N-2r)\), with a plateau at \(1/N\) when \((N-2r)^2\ge N\) and an adjusted endpoint-count construction in the strict regime. The formulation allows nonexchangeable assignment laws and assignment-dependent weights. At exact balance, the established finite vertex certificate describes all optimizers; the proved six-moment Gram proposition gives an equivalent representation, and uniform balanced randomization admits the sharp nonzero constant-shift interval \(|\kappa|\le\kappa_N\) for every even \(N\). A structural classification of arbitrary nonconstant shifts and nonuniform balanced laws remains open. The pseudo-unit bijection expresses the experiment as a calibrated one-total problem on one-per-pair samples.
gap: Published causal minimax results identify the unrestricted Bernoulli value and the uniform exact-balance value, while generalized-Bernoulli sampling already supplies bounded-count pairwise-independent constructions. Gabler (1990) solves several one-population-total cuboid games, and Gabler and Stenger (2000) treat arbitrary sample sizes for one-total centered quadratic spaces. The current unresolved question is the paired-potential-outcome causal saddle for an almost-sure intermediate treated-count band, its assignment-dependent estimator adjustment, and its optimizer geometry without exchangeability, fair marginals, or design unbiasedness.
fill: Prove the two-branch minimax formula by an analytic no-effect least-favorable prior and a matching diamond-box endpoint-count construction; prove necessary-and-sufficient optimizer conditions on the plateau and strict nonsingular faces; give an explicit orientation counterexample to second-moment sufficiency; and reduce the singular balanced face to scalar shifts while leaving its final structural classification as a named open question.
